subject.title: [Field Report] Chrome 136+ binds CDP to [::1] (IPv6) on Windows — portproxy v4tov4 breaks silently

question: What exact Chrome/WSL2 wording and proof bar should OpenClaw require before updating the WSL2 remote-CDP guide and empty-reply diagnostic?
rationale: A prior fix was closed because it described the behavior as a universal Chrome 136+ invariant, but current docs and diagnostics still omit the observed [::1]/v4tov6 failure mode.

options.title: Approve scoped diagnostic wording
options.body: Land a narrow docs and diagnostic update that describes the IPv4/IPv6 split as an observed host state, preserves the self-loop warning, and avoids a WSL-side [::1] auto-probe.

options.title: Require live affected-host proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open until someone captures real Windows/WSL2 Chrome proof for the exact version and portproxy behavior maintainers want documented.

options.title: Defer to docs only
options.body: Update only the troubleshooting guide and leave runtime diagnostic text unchanged if maintainers do not want Chromium-version-specific guidance in product output.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped diagnostic wording
recommendation.body: Land a narrow docs and diagnostic update that describes the IPv4/IPv6 split as an observed host state, preserves the self-loop warning, and avoids a WSL-side [::1] auto-probe.

likelyOwner.reason: He made the most recent explicit scope decision on the closed attempted fix and named the proof concern.
